A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoSciDACT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. The material aligns reliably; v2's additional page results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection experiments in Figure 3 and additional empirical studies, including butterfly hybrids, CIFAR distribution shifts, and CMS Higgs data in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including the main benchmark results and all appendix studies.

M1.justification: The contrastive encoder, auxiliary cross-entropy objective, NPLM hypothesis test, and kernel-combination procedure remain identical. Neither the main text nor the appendices introduce a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic, LIGO, JetClass, histology, CIFAR, and butterfly data, including the same CIFAR distribution-shift and CMS Higgs-search scenarios in Appendices D and E.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: supervised and ideal-supervised tests, Mahalanobis, MMD, Fréchet, one-class SVM, and the Higgs mass-fit comparison are retained in their corresponding experiments. The replacement of reference [12] adds no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 1's sample sizes and injection fractions, Appendix A's splits and training settings, and the evaluation procedures in Section 5 and Appendices B–E are unchanged.

E4.justification: The synthetic-data analyses, kernel-width and embedding-dimension scans, label-noise tests, distribution-shift experiments, and Higgs case study are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Pseudo-experiment counts, empirical and asymptotic significance calculations, and uncertainty displays are unchanged, including the 500-toy protocol and empirical Z-score ceiling described with Figure 3.

E6.justification: The result figures and numerical findings match throughout. For example, Figure 15(c) retains observed p = 0.116 and expected p = 0.162 for standard AutoSciDACT; the main and supplementary sensitivity curves also remain identical.

T1.justification: The loss definitions, likelihood-ratio formulation, NPLM estimator, significance calculations, and baseline mathematics are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and Section 6.3 conclusion are unchanged, retaining the same claims about a transferable scientific novelty-discovery pipeline and sensitivity to small anomalous signals.

C2.justification: Scientific interpretations and limitations concerning label quality, embedding dimensionality, limited samples, and domain shift remain unchanged. The new acknowledgment explains a bibliography error rather than revising the interpretation or limitations of the research.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, and timing information remain identical. Reference [99] switches between DOI and record URLs identifying the same Zenodo record; no different resource or access arrangement is documented.

R1.justification: Reference [12] changes from 'Mineclip' (2022) to Azabou et al., 'Mine your own view: Self-supervised learning through across-sample prediction' (2021). v2 identifies the former entry as AI-hallucinated and the replacement as the intended source. This is a limited citation replacement; Section 2's positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 7 adds a paragraph acknowledging the erroneous reference and explaining its generation through an LLM. Other edits update the version header, author formatting in reference [63], and BioCLIP's publication metadata in [116]. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment and revised reference entries reflow the bibliography, placing its final two entries on a largely empty additional page. Figures 1–16 and Table 1 retain identical content, captions, and layouts; appendix pagination shifts.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces the citation it explicitly acknowledges as AI-hallucinated with the intended reference and explains the error in Section 7. This provides a limited improvement in attribution and transparency. The scientific methods, evidence, conclusions, and limitations remain unchanged.
